source.publication: Information for retired persons (NYS Department of Taxation and Finance)
source.section: Subtractions, Railroad Retirement benefits (Tier 2 benefits under the Railroad Retirement Act of 1974, subtracted on Form IT-225 code S-122, carried to Form IT-201 line 31); Form IT-201 lines 19, 31-39; IT-201-I PDF page 11 (line 34) and PDF pages 12 and 33 (line 39)

worked: Single, 66: Railroad Retirement Tier 2 benefits 30,000 (no Tier 1 benefit in this case), taxable interest 55,000 (not U.S. obligations), dividends 20,000. Federal AGI = 30,000 + 55,000 + 20,000 = 105,000. Tier 2 is exempt from state tax under Title 45 U.S.C. and is not line 29 pension income here, since it is subtracted in full. Federal AGI (IT-201 line 19) = 105,000.00. Federal taxable income = 105,000.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction - 1 x 2,000 age-65 addition = 87,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Subtraction: line 31 (IT-225 S-122) Tier 2 railroad retirement benefits included in federal AGI, in full 30,000.00. Line 32 total subtractions = 30,000.00. Line 33 New York AGI = 105,000.00 - 30,000.00 = 75,000.00. Line 34 New York standard deduction (single, PDF page 11 table) 8,000.00; line 35 = 75,000.00 - 8,000.00 = 67,000.00; line 36 dependent exemption 0 (no dependents); lines 37/38 taxable income 67,000.00. Rate schedule (PDF page 33, single) on 67,000.00: 8,500.00 x 4% = 340.00; 3,200.00 x 4.5% = 144.00; 2,200.00 x 5.25% = 115.50; 53,100.00 x 5.5% = 2,920.50; schedule tax = 3,520.00 (the printed schedule, with its whole-dollar base 600 at 13,900, gives 3,520.50; this case uses the bands as numbers). NY AGI is 107,650 or less and line 38 is 65,000 or more: the rate schedule applies (PDF page 12, line 39); no recapture worksheet. Line 39 NYS tax = 3,520.00. Credits: none (the household credit, line 40, PDF page 12 tables 1-3, allows no credit above federal AGI of 28,000 single or 32,000 other statuses): state income tax = 3,520.00.
